purpose: G1's OWN corpus extension, kept separate from G0's frozen corpus so G0's frozen digest stays valid and its acceptance is not disturbed. These cover the sufficiency conditions #50 lists that G0's dimensions do not reach.

mutants.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::topLevel
mutants.dimension: extension member added elsewhere in the library
mutants.note: sufficiency: extension members must not disturb an unrelated declaration's identity

mutants.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::topLevel
mutants.note: MUST move: a renamed declaration is a different declaration

mutants.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::topLevel
mutants.note: MUST move: kind is part of the identity, and the VM name changes too (topLevel -> get:topLevel)

mutants.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::topLevel
mutants.dimension: the subject is re-owned (top level -> static member of Shape)
mutants.note: MUST move: owner path is part of the identity

mutants.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::topLevel
mutants.dimension: the subject moves to a different library
mutants.note: MUST move. Worth stating plainly: this means renaming a package re-identifies every declaration in it, which is a real design consequence for SM1-G6 to weigh, not a defect of the identity.

mutants.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::ShapeX.doubled
mutants.dimension: two same-named extension members in DIFFERENT extensions
mutants.note: Not a stability case. The claim is DISTINCTNESS: ShapeX.doubled and BoxX.doubled must get different identities, and they must differ by OWNER rather than by accident of the kernel's `ShapeX|doubled` mangling. Scored by the distinctness arm, not by comparison to base.

mutants.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::ShapeX.doubled
mutants.note: MUST move: the owner path is part of the identity, and the extension is the owner.

mutants.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::Box.unwrap
mutants.dimension: the owner's generic BOUND changes; the member is the subject
mutants.note: MUST stay stable. `Box.unwrap` was not renamed, re-owned or re-kinded, so it is the same declaration. Whether it is still ABI-compatible is SM1-G2's question -- G1 must not smuggle ABI semantics into identity.

mutants.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::topLevel
mutants.dimension: a LOCAL (nested) function inside the subject
mutants.note: The enclosing declaration keeps its identity. Whether the nested function is NAMED at all is a separate scope claim, checked by the nested-scope arm.

mutants.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::topLevel
mutants.dimension: synthetic/generated members appear (implicit ctor, mixin forwarders)
mutants.note: The unrelated subject must not move. What the walker NAMES among the generated members, and how it flags them, is checked by the synthetic arm.

baseline_note: Each case compares against `base` unless it names a `baseline`. ext_extension_owner_renamed must compare against ext_extension_member, because base declares no extension at all and the subject does not exist there.
destination_note: A must-move case declares expected_new_subject. Disappearance from the old key is NOT sufficient evidence that identity moved -- a walker that simply dropped the declaration would satisfy it. The scorer requires: old key absent, the expected new key present EXACTLY ONCE, and the new declaration_id different from the old one.

scope_expectations.why: The accepted scope is that local/nested functions are NOT independently addressable. named != 0 must FAIL until that scope is deliberately changed, not merely reported as a FINDING.

required_synthetic_row.why: The implicit constructor the CFE generates must be present AND flagged. An arm that fails only when NO generated members are found can green with flagged_synthetic == 0, which would let the flag rot unnoticed.
